text: Using HTTPS is essential for any modern website. It encrypts data exchanged between the user’s browser and the server, preventing hackers from stealing sensitive information like passwords or credit card numbers. Another crucial layer is authentication, which ensures that only authorized users can access certain parts of an application. Strong passwords and multi-factor authentication significantly reduce the risk of unauthorized access. However, even with these measures, developers must also practice input validation. This means checking and sanitizing all user-submitted data before processing it. Without it, common vulnerabilities like SQL injection or cross-site scripting (XSS) can occur, allowing attackers to manipulate databases or inject malicious scripts. Ultimately, security is an ongoing responsibility, not a one-time setup.
